node_definition.done_when: tests/test_a_launched_run_reads_launched.py passes at head. It serves a fixture project whose live pointer has a live supervisor pid and no stream file, and asserts that GET /crew reports that run in the same phase the crew live view classification gives it, not idle. It also asserts a run with a fresh stream reads working, and a terminal one done. The test reads no state outside its temporary home. Every test file naming _crew_rows, _log_activity or the /crew route passes at head, with base and head arms over that population recorded.
node_definition.goal: Read section 3 of the-restarted-server-meets-its-shipped-measures first, then the measurement it cites in docs/evidence/fragments/the-restarted-server-meets-its-shipped-measures/live-server-measures.html. Make GET /crew report each run's phase from the same classification the crew live view uses, never from a second rule. Today reckon/serve.py (the rows loop near _log_activity and _stream_is_terminal) derives done, working or idle from the age of the run's stream file. A launched run therefore reads idle for 15 to 45 s until its worker writes a stream. The crew live view classifies a pointer through reckon/crew/recovery.py. Its row phase must carry over, including the state of a launched run whose supervisor is live and whose stream does not exist yet, which must not read idle. Keep the response fields the SPA reads, adding none it does not need. The SPA renders the phase it is given. Leave GET /crew's response time to a later node, but report the time your fixture's request takes. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/the-restarted-server-meets-its-shipped-measures/a-launched-run-reads-launched.html.
